correctness.rationale: Stepwise proof: involutive-letter reverse-subset construction is DUFA, group transitivity distinguishes distinct subsets, orbit-stabilizer gives exact complexity; explicit three involutions generate S_n; subgroup of two involutions is cyclic-by-two and transitive order <=2n; for n4 orbit six cannot divide order4/8, for n5 all pairs have a reflection stabilizer; n>=6 central binomial exceeds 2n. The actual embedded verifier independently checks 36 n,m configurations, 118080 words and 159 exhaustive transitive binary pairs. No finite-to-infinite inference is made.

originality.rationale: The reviewed Acta Informatica article expressly leaves DUFA reversal closure and state complexity open for multiple accepting states; a full-text implication comparison with the broader permutation-automaton theorem verifies that its binomial bound is inherited but its witness violates involutive generator restrictions. The new result supplies three involutive generators, the exact orbit formula for DUFA and the lower bound proving three letters necessary for central extremality for every n >= 4. value.rationale: Kutrib–Malcher–Schneider expressly posed DUFA reversal closure and state complexity as open in the 2021 full article. The theorem resolves both for all minimal n-state DUFA, gives a usable exact orbit invariant for each automaton, and establishes a sharp qualitative 3-vs-2 input-letter difference from the previously known general PFA reversal bound. The distinction has an infinite family, sharp all-n claims and motivated complexity interpretation, not a renamed special case.
